darkcraft.diario.capitulo7: By the Arch of the Threshold, Maelis told me what Morvain was before the red sky: bells, mills, harbours. Its people did not die: they stayed, bound to the last thing they swore.
darkcraft.diario.capitulo8: Before the fallen statue of the Capital, Maelis told me of those who stayed: the Constable who shut the gates, the Rector, the Abbot, the ferryman, Brann, Anselmo. She asked me to remember their names.
darkcraft.diario.capitulo9: In Aldric's hut I learned he was the first marked one. He climbed the southern chain and there was no door at the top: only a mouth, waiting. The Shadow does not want its chains broken: it wants a living hand to open a door.
darkcraft.diario.capitulo10: Beside the Last Flame, Maelis told me her sisters forged the eight chains with the fire of their souls, and that every shrine is one of them. She is the last. She cannot choose for me.
darkcraft.ayuda.cronica: The chronicle of Morvain: where the chests of chapters 7-10 are, take you to one, place them now or forget them (to place them again)
darkcraft.dialogo.hagen.1: Another marked one, still breathing. Sit by the fire, if you like. I'm Hagen. I shod the Constable's horses... back when there were horses.
darkcraft.dialogo.hagen.2: Back again? The fire's still going. So am I.
darkcraft.dialogo.hagen.3: Let's see what you've been swinging.
darkcraft.dialogo.hagen.5: Not enough. Stones for the steel, echoes for the fire. Come back when you've got both.
darkcraft.dialogo.hagen.6: When the Shadow came, I ran. Hammer on my back, anvil on a cart. Left everything else behind... even my apprentice, Tobin. Useless boy. I hope he's still alive.
darkcraft.dialogo.hagen.7: Go on, then. Try not to come back in pieces.
darkcraft.dialogo.hagen.8: That blade has nothing left to learn from me.
darkcraft.dialogo.hagen.9: Ashes of war? Bring them to me. Steel remembers how its old masters fought... I only remind it.
darkcraft.dialogo.hagen.op.mejorar: I want to improve my weapon or my armor.
darkcraft.dialogo.hagen.op.cenizas: Tell me about ashes of war.
darkcraft.dialogo.hagen.op.refugio: Why are you in this refuge?
darkcraft.dialogo.brenna.1: Careful where you step, that's my good anvil. I'm Brenna. I mend what the sea spits back... hooks, chains, swords. Mostly swords, these days.
darkcraft.dialogo.brenna.2: Still in one piece? The tide's been kinder to you than to most.
darkcraft.dialogo.brenna.3: Right. Let's have a look at it.
darkcraft.dialogo.brenna.4: Salt-tempered. It won't rust, and it won't forgive.
darkcraft.dialogo.brenna.5: I can't forge with good intentions. Stones and echoes, love.
darkcraft.dialogo.brenna.6: My father built ships in the old port, before the whaler lost his mind and the harbour drowned. Now I mend whatever keeps the next fool alive.
darkcraft.dialogo.brenna.7: Mind the gulls. They've developed a taste for people.
darkcraft.dialogo.brenna.8: That's as good as steel gets. Even out here.
darkcraft.dialogo.brenna.op.mejorar: I want to improve my weapon or my armor.
darkcraft.dialogo.brenna.op.historia: How did you end up here?
darkcraft.dialogo.ulrik.1: Ha! A traveller, up here, in this cold! Come, warm your hands at my forge. I am Ulrik. The mountain took my toes, but not my arms!
darkcraft.dialogo.ulrik.2: Back from the snow! Good. Fewer frozen corpses for me to bury.
darkcraft.dialogo.ulrik.4: Ha! Forged in snow and fire. Now it sings!
darkcraft.dialogo.ulrik.5: No, no. The forge eats echoes, friend, and stones. You have not enough of either.
darkcraft.dialogo.ulrik.6: Up there, past the fang, sleeps the ash dragon. When it roars, the whole mountain shakes. Ha! I've lost two anvils to the avalanches already!
darkcraft.dialogo.ulrik.7: Go! And if you see the dragon... run faster than I did!
darkcraft.dialogo.ulrik.8: Nothing more to give it. Not even the mountain could make it better!
darkcraft.dialogo.ulrik.op.mejorar: I want to improve my weapon or my armor.
darkcraft.dialogo.tobin.1: Oh! A customer! A real one! I'm Tobin, I'm a smith! Well, an apprentice. Well, I was. Master Hagen said I was hopeless, but he's not here, so...
darkcraft.dialogo.tobin.2: You came back! Nobody comes back!
darkcraft.dialogo.tobin.3: Okay, okay, let me see it! I'll be careful, I promise!
darkcraft.dialogo.tobin.4: It worked! I mean, of course it worked. It worked!
darkcraft.dialogo.tobin.5: Sorry, sorry! I need more stones... and echoes. Master Hagen never forged for free, so neither do I.
darkcraft.dialogo.tobin.6: I was in the Capital when the Constable shut the gates. I hid in a chimney for three days. I'm still a bit sooty, actually.
darkcraft.dialogo.tobin.7: Bye! Don't die! Please don't die!
darkcraft.dialogo.tobin.8: That's... that's the best thing I've ever made. Don't tell Master Hagen I said that.
darkcraft.dialogo.tobin.op.mejorar: I want to improve my weapon or my armor.
darkcraft.dialogo.silas.1: Ah! A customer, in Morvain! Silas, at your service. Whatever the dead left behind, I sell... at a very fair price.
darkcraft.dialogo.silas.2: Still alive? Good, good. The crows are terrible customers.
darkcraft.dialogo.silas.4: Echoes, friend. I don't take promises... or teeth.
darkcraft.dialogo.silas.5: Where next? Wherever the road is quiet. I never stay long in one place. Look for me by the shrines.
darkcraft.dialogo.silas.6: They say the Shadow can't see a man who keeps moving. So far, so good.

advancements.darkcraft.hagen.description: Talk to Hagen, the smith of the refuge
advancements.darkcraft.herreros.title: The Anvils of Morvain
advancements.darkcraft.herreros.descript: Talk to the four smiths of Morvain: Hagen, Brenna, Ulrik and Tobin
advancements.darkcraft.silas.title: A Customer in Morvain
advancements.darkcraft.silas.description: Find Silas, the merchant who wanders from shrine to shrine
darkcraft.diario.refugio: North of the Pilgrims' Crossroads there is a house with its chimney still smoking: the Forge Refuge. Inside, someone is still striking an anvil.
darkcraft.diario.hagen: Hagen used to shoe the Constable's horses. When the Shadow came he fled with his hammer and his anvil, and left even his apprentice behind. He keeps forging by the fire.
darkcraft.diario.herreros: I have met the four smiths of Morvain: Hagen in his refuge, Brenna at the harbour, Ulrik on the mountain and Tobin at the gates of the Capital. Tobin was Hagen's apprentice. Neither of them knows the other is still alive.
darkcraft.diario.silas: A merchant with an eyepatch trades by the shrines. His name is Silas, and he says the Shadow cannot see a man who keeps moving. He never stays long anywhere.
darkcraft.diario.silas_compra: I bought something from Silas. He swore it was a very fair price. He counted the coins twice.
darkcraft.ayuda.herreros: The smiths of Morvain: how they are, take you to one's forge, place them now or forget them (to place them again)
darkcraft.ayuda.silas: Silas, the wandering merchant: where he is and where he goes next, take you to him or move him along his route
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.1: Who's there? ...Footsteps. And ash. You carry a flame, don't you? Forgive an old man, flame-bearer. I've lost my bell... and without it, the dead won't let me pass.
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.2: Bless you. The hanged ones of the dead wood took it, far to the west. It hangs where the oldest tree bends over the road. Listen for it... when the wind passes, it still rings.
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.3: A blind pilgrim owns very little. But I carry the rosary of my order... bone beads, worn smooth by forty years of prayer. Bring me the bell, and it's yours.
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.4: Then go your way. The roads are long in these lands... and in the end, the bells toll for everyone.
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.5: You came back... but I don't hear it. The dead wood lies to the west. Follow the road where the trees wear ropes.
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.6: Ah. The one who walked past. Have you changed your mind, flame-bearer?
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.7: That sound... That's my bell! You found it. Please... let me hold it.
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.8: There. Do you hear them? The pilgrims... all of them, walking north at last. Take the rosary, flame-bearer. May the road be kind to you.
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.9: And you asked for nothing. Few do, in these lands. Take my order's alms as well. The dead would want them spent on the living.
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.10: No... no, please! Without it, I... Then you're no better than the hanged ones. Keep it. And may the dead follow you, as they followed me.
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.11: ...I have nothing more to say to you.
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.12: I can still hear them walking. Thank you, flame-bearer. Go with the light.
darkcraft.dialogo.oswin.op.precio: What will you give me for it?
darkcraft.mision.oswin.pendiente: Oswin, a blind pilgrim waiting by the Pilgrims' Crossroads, lost his bell: without it, he says, the dead won't let him pass. You can still help him.
darkcraft.mision.oswin.buscar: Oswin, the blind pilgrim of the Crossroads, lost his bell: the hanged ones of the Dead Wood took it. It hangs from the oldest tree of the Hanged Grove, where it bends over the road; when the wind passes, it rings.
darkcraft.mision.oswin.volver: You carry Oswin's bell. Take it back to him at the Pilgrims' Crossroads: he will decide... or you will.
darkcraft.mision.oswin.encontrada: You found a pilgrim's hand bell hanging from the Gallows Tree. Someone must miss it: a blind pilgrim waits by the Pilgrims' Crossroads.
darkcraft.mision.oswin.devuelta: You gave Oswin back his bell. He rang it, and the dead pilgrims set off north at last. He gave you the rosary of his order.
darkcraft.mision.oswin.quedada: You kept Oswin's bell. He is still at the Crossroads, with no one to guide him. Now the dead follow you.
darkcraft.mision.oswin.ir.buscar: The bell hangs here: the Gallows Tree
darkcraft.mision.oswin.ir.volver: Oswin waits at the Pilgrims' Crossroads
darkcraft.mision.oswin.ir.encontrada: A blind pilgrim waits at the Crossroads
darkcraft.mision.oswin.ir.pendiente: Oswin waits at the Pilgrims' Crossroads
darkcraft.mision.oswin.cogida: You have the pilgrim's bell: take it back to Oswin at the Pilgrims' Crossroads.
darkcraft.mision.oswin.cogida_sin: A pilgrim's hand bell. Someone must be missing it...
darkcraft.mision.oswin.ya: The bell is no longer yours to take.
item.darkcraft.campana_peregrino.desc: A little bronze bell, green with rust. With it, the dead pilgrims used to find their way.
item.darkcraft.campana_difuntos.desc: Oswin's bell, which guides no one now. Ring it: the dead around you shrink away, slow and weak, for a few seconds.
subtitles.darkcraft.sfx.campana_viento: A small bell rings in the wind
darkcraft.diario.campana_peregrino: I gave Oswin, the blind pilgrim, his bell back. He rang it, and the dead who could not pass set off north, praying. He gave me the rosary of his order.
darkcraft.diario.campana_difuntos: I kept Oswin's bell. He called me worse than the hanged ones. When I ring it, the dead shrink away... and he is left alone at the Crossroads.
darkcraft.ayuda.misiones: Quests: how they stand, forget them or set Oswin's, Hedda's, Ylva's, Corwen's or Sigrun's
darkcraft.ayuda.oswin: Oswin and his bell: where they are, take you to him or under the bell, place them now or forget them
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.1: Oh... you're going to the gate, aren't you, child? My Tam keeps it. The night the sky turned red, they shut it... and he never came home. Would you look for him? He wears a red scarf. I knitted it myself.
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.2: Bless you, child. The guards kept a room above the arch, by the winch. Bring me back something of his... anything at all.
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.3: The Constable had every gate shut, so the fire wouldn't spread. Folk ran for the West Gate... I could hear them from the road. My Tam was on watch that night.
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.4: Then I'll keep waiting. I've gotten good at it.
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.5: The room above the arch, child. By the winch. Have you been up there yet?
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.6: You came back. Will you look for my Tam now?
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.7: That's... that's his scarf. Where is he? No... Tell me, child. How did my boy die?
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.8: ...Then he did as he was told. Like I taught him. Oh, Tam... Someone has to close his eyes. I'll go to him.
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.9: Pull his spear out of that wheel, child. He's held it long enough.
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.10: I knew it. I knew my Tam. Give it here... There. Thank you, child. I can stop waiting now.
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.11: Then he's still out there somewhere. I'll knit him another. The winters here are long.
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.12: Any word of my Tam? ...No. Well. I'll keep knitting.
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.13: Go on, child. I'll stay with him now. He always got cold, my Tam.
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.14: That scarf... I'd know my own stitches anywhere. That's my Tam's! Where did you find it? Tell me... how did my boy die?
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.op.verdad: He held the gate shut. By order.
darkcraft.dialogo.hedda.op.mentira: He died trying to open it.
darkcraft.mision.hedda.pendiente: Hedda knits on the road to the West Gate of the Capital, facing the gate. Her son Tam kept it the night of the red sky and never came home. You can still look for him.
darkcraft.mision.hedda.buscar: Hedda is waiting for her son Tam, who kept the West Gate of the Capital. The guards had their room above the arch, by the portcullis winch: you go up through the north tower, from inside the wall. Tam wears a red scarf.
darkcraft.mision.hedda.volver: You found Tam in the guard room, sitting with his back to the winch, his spear thrust through the wheel: no one was going to raise the gate. Take his scarf to Hedda... and decide what you tell her.
darkcraft.mision.hedda.encontrada: A red scarf, knitted by hand, around the neck of a dead guard by the winch of the West Gate. Someone knitted it for him: on the road to the gate, an old woman knits and waits.
darkcraft.mision.hedda.lanza: You told Hedda the truth: that Tam held the gate shut, by order. She has gone to him in the guard room. She asked you to pull his spear out of the winch wheel.
darkcraft.mision.hedda.verdad: You told Hedda the truth. Now she keeps watch over her son in the guard room, by the winch. You pulled Tam's spear out of the wheel.
darkcraft.mision.hedda.mentira: You told Hedda that Tam died trying to open the gate. She put on his scarf, stopped waiting and faded away in peace. She left you her blessing.
darkcraft.mision.hedda.callada: You told Hedda you didn't find Tam. She is still knitting on the road, waiting for him. His scarf stayed with you.
darkcraft.mision.hedda.ir.buscar: The guard room, above the West Gate
darkcraft.mision.hedda.ir.volver: Hedda waits on the road to the West Gate
darkcraft.mision.hedda.ir.encontrada: An old woman knits on the road to the West Gate
darkcraft.mision.hedda.ir.pendiente: Hedda waits on the road to the West Gate
darkcraft.mision.hedda.ir.lanza: Tam's spear, in the winch wheel
darkcraft.mision.hedda.cogida: You have Tam's red scarf: go back to Hedda, on the road to the West Gate.
darkcraft.mision.hedda.cogida_sin: A red scarf, knitted by hand. Someone knitted it for him...
darkcraft.mision.hedda.nada: There is nothing left to take.
darkcraft.mision.hedda.lanza_cogida: You pulled the spear out of the wheel.
item.darkcraft.bufanda_roja.desc: Red wool knitted by hand, with the tight stitches of someone who knits in winter. It was around the neck of a West Gate guard, fallen by the portcullis winch with his spear thrust through the wheel: no one was going to raise the gate.
item.darkcraft.lanza_tam.desc: Tam's spear, of the West Gate watch. It held shut a gate that no one should have shut. Scales with Strength (C) and Dexterity (B).
item.darkcraft.talisman_madre.desc: If a blow leaves you below a quarter of your health, it heals you 30% (once every two minutes).
item.darkcraft.talisman_bufanda.desc: Blocking costs 30% less stamina and fire hurts you 20% less.
subtitles.darkcraft.sfx.lanza_sacar: A spear comes out of a wooden wheel
advancements.darkcraft.hedda_verdad.desc: Tell Hedda how her son really died
advancements.darkcraft.hedda_mentira.des: Tell Hedda her son died trying to open the gate
advancements.darkcraft.hedda_callar.desc: Keep Tam's scarf without telling Hedda anything
darkcraft.diario.hedda_verdad: I told Hedda the truth: that her son held the West Gate shut while people burned, because he was ordered to. She went to close his eyes. She asked me to pull his spear out of the wheel.
darkcraft.diario.hedda_mentira: I told Hedda that Tam died trying to open the gate. She believed me. She put on his scarf, smiled, and faded like a lantern at dawn. Sometimes a lie is all you can give.
darkcraft.diario.hedda_callar: I told Hedda I didn't find her son. I kept his scarf. She is still knitting on the road to the West Gate, and she will keep waiting.
darkcraft.ayuda.hedda: Hedda and Tam: where they are, take you to her or to the guard room, place them now or forget them
darkcraft.diario.armadura_jefe: I put on the armor of a boss I defeated. It weighs more than it should: something of him is still inside.
darkcraft.ayuda.armadura_jefes: The boss sets you have already been given (and forget them to try again)
advancements.darkcraft.mejora_armadura.d: Upgrade a piece of armor at a blacksmith's forge
darkcraft.diario.mejora_armadura: A smith hammered my armor into shape. Now it stops what it didn't before.
darkcraft.ayuda.armadura_mejora: Set the armor you are wearing to +n (from +0 to +5)
item.darkcraft.caballero_yelmo.desc: Closed helm of the Valdrenn guard, with its visor slit and the red plume of those who swore.
item.darkcraft.caballero_peto.desc: Plate cuirass under the red tabard with the golden crown. It weighs like an oath.
item.darkcraft.caballero_guantes.desc: Lamed gauntlets. With them a sword is held even when the arm trembles.
item.darkcraft.caballero_grebas.desc: Cuisses, knee cops and greaves with a fauld of lames. Made for never stepping back.
item.darkcraft.confesor_yelmo.desc: Black hood over a closed helm. The confessors heard sins without showing their faces.
item.darkcraft.confesor_peto.desc: Blackened plate with the purple tabard and the silver crown of those who forgave.
item.darkcraft.confesor_guantes.desc: Blackened gauntlets. They blessed and strangled with the same hand.
item.darkcraft.confesor_grebas.desc: Dark greaves of the court confessors, who entered the cells without a sound.
item.darkcraft.vagabundo_yelmo.desc: Spangenhelm with brass bands and a nasal, over a mail coif. It has seen many roads.
item.darkcraft.vagabundo_peto.desc: Mail over a padded gambeson. Patched so many times it now belongs to whoever wears it.
item.darkcraft.vagabundo_guantes.desc: Leather gloves with plates on the back.
item.darkcraft.vagabundo_grebas.desc: Hose and tall leather boots, worn at the toes.
item.darkcraft.guerrero_yelmo.desc: Mail coif with a blue cloth band tied at the nape.
item.darkcraft.guerrero_peto.desc: Mail over the blue gambeson of those who fought with a weapon in each hand.
item.darkcraft.guerrero_guantes.desc: Tanned leather gloves made for never letting go of two swords.
item.darkcraft.guerrero_grebas.desc: Leather boots of the northern warriors, who never stood still.
item.darkcraft.barbaro_yelmo.desc: Iron skullcap with a fur rim and two horns from a beast that no longer exists.
item.darkcraft.barbaro_peto.desc: Open leather vest with a bearskin mantle and a bone pauldron. Warm against the cold of the peaks.
item.darkcraft.barbaro_guantes.desc: Studded leather bracers with fur cuffs.
item.darkcraft.barbaro_grebas.desc: Fur leggings bound with straps, with a loincloth and a bone-buckled belt.
item.darkcraft.bandido_yelmo.desc: Black hood and a mask up to the nose: only the eyes show, and never the same ones.
item.darkcraft.bandido_peto.desc: Studded black leather jerkin with a bandolier of knives and a short cape.
item.darkcraft.bandido_guantes.desc: Strapped leather bracers. Fingers bare, for the knife and other people's purses.
item.darkcraft.bandido_grebas.desc: Dark hose and tall buckled boots. They make no sound.
item.darkcraft.hechicero_yelmo.desc: Pointed hat with a silver band and a glintstone. The Academy wore it crooked.
item.darkcraft.hechicero_peto.desc: High-collared blue robe with wide sleeves and a silver trim. Guards against magic more than steel.
item.darkcraft.hechicero_guantes.desc: Thin black silk gloves, with a blue stone ring.
item.darkcraft.hechicero_grebas.desc: Long skirts with the purple sash of those who studied the stars.
item.darkcraft.profeta_yelmo.desc: A blindfold stained with dried blood. Prophets covered their eyes to see what is coming.
item.darkcraft.profeta_peto.desc: Reddish robe with a mantle of black feathers. It smells of candle smoke.
item.darkcraft.profeta_guantes.desc: Wraps around the wrists and a string of bone beads.
item.darkcraft.profeta_grebas.desc: Frayed reddish skirts and feet bandaged from so much walking.
item.darkcraft.prisionero_yelmo.desc: An iron cage padlocked around the head. Someone wanted you never to forget your crime.
item.darkcraft.prisionero_peto.desc: Patched sackcloth rags. What is left of what you wore the day they locked you up.
item.darkcraft.prisionero_guantes.desc: Iron shackles without a chain. The chain broke; they didn't.
item.darkcraft.prisionero_grebas.desc: Torn hose and dirty wraps around the feet.
item.darkcraft.capitan_yelmo.desc: The three-cornered hat of Edrik Maroll, captain of the Grey Heron, with gold braid that no longer shines.
item.darkcraft.capitan_peto.desc: Blue coat with gold buttons and a red sash. It smells of salt and seaweed: it spent a long time at the bottom.
item.darkcraft.capitan_guantes.desc: Leather gloves with embroidered cuffs. They gripped the helm until the ship stopped being a ship.
item.darkcraft.capitan_grebas.desc: Dark breeches and tall cuffed boots, still holding sand from the bottom of the pier.
item.darkcraft.brandt_yelmo.desc: Closed helm of black iron with its studded ring and spikes. Through the slit, only two embers could be seen.
item.darkcraft.brandt_peto.desc: Thick black plate under the red tabard with the tower. He was King Corvin's shield in life and his wall in death.
item.darkcraft.brandt_guantes.desc: Black gauntlets with golden knuckles. They held the pavise as if it weighed nothing.
item.darkcraft.brandt_grebas.desc: Black plate greaves and fauld. Ser Brandt never took a step back; neither should you.
item.darkcraft.vareth_yelmo.desc: Bark that grew over a helm until the helm belonged to the tree. Branches sprout from it like antlers.
item.darkcraft.vareth_peto.desc: Bark plates with moss and a green heart that still beats. Vareth guarded the tree for so long that the tree kept him.
item.darkcraft.vareth_guantes.desc: Bark gauntlets with three root claws. The bark wants nothing to do with fire.
item.darkcraft.vareth_grebas.desc: Bark greaves wrapped in roots. Sometimes, if you stand still, they try to take root.
item.darkcraft.rey_yelmo.desc: Black helm with the eight-pointed golden crown. Embers still glow through the slit.
item.darkcraft.rey_peto.desc: Black plate with gold trim, an ermine capelet and the crimson tabard with the crown; on the back, the king's cape.
item.darkcraft.rey_guantes.desc: Black and gold gauntlets. They held two swords of fire through centuries of waiting.
item.darkcraft.rey_grebas.desc: Black greaves with gold trim. The king of Valdrenn did not rise from his throne for centuries; when he did, everything burned.
item.darkcraft.gavran_yelmo.desc: Ser Gavran's helm, with its crown of roots and the slit that glows green. He kept his oath to the very end.
item.darkcraft.gavran_peto.desc: Old black steel with moss and the red tabard bearing the sword of the oath. The King's champion wore it when there was no king left.
item.darkcraft.gavran_guantes.desc: Old steel gauntlets wrapped in roots. They never let go of the greatsword, not even when his heart was already wood.
item.darkcraft.gavran_grebas.desc: Black steel greaves with coiled roots. The roots are still growing, slowly.
darkcraft.ayuda.armadura: Armor: the list, give yourself a set or a piece, put on a whole set
item.darkcraft.maza.desc: A steel head with six flanges and a brass neck. The clerics of Valdrenn said it shed no blood; it broke bones. Scales with Faith.
item.darkcraft.martillo_guerra.desc: A square head on one side and a spike on the other, on a long haft with iron rings. It was made for those who wore plate.
item.darkcraft.gran_martillo.desc: A block of carved stone with iron bands and a red rune. It takes both hands and your whole back; what it hits does not get up again.
darkcraft.martillo.guardia: Breaks shield guards and hits armored foes harder.
item.darkcraft.flecha_fuego.desc: A pitch-soaked rag behind the head: it catches fire as it flies and sets its target ablaze.
item.darkcraft.flecha_sangre.desc: A serrated bone head. Each one opens a wound: at the third, the hemorrhage tears away a good share of life.
item.darkcraft.flecha_escarcha.desc: A head of ice that never melts. Each one builds up cold: at the third it bursts, slows, and the victim takes more damage for a while.
darkcraft.flecha.mano: Equip them in your left hand to shoot them with a bow or crossbow.
darkcraft.ayuda.armas: Weapons: the hammers, the special arrows with bow and crossbow, add bleed or frost to what is in front of you
item.darkcraft.rodela.desc: A small round walnut shield with an iron rim and boss. It does not stop everything, but it rises in the blink of an eye.
item.darkcraft.escudo_caballero.desc: The heater shield of the knights of Valdrenn, the golden crown upon red. It stops everything.
item.darkcraft.paves.desc: A wall of crimson wood with black iron bands, as tall as a man. The archers of the guard hid behind it.
darkcraft.escudo.parada: Raised at the right instant it stops the whole blow and staggers the attacker. You move faster while guarding.
darkcraft.escudo.paves: Guarding with it barely tires you, but it weighs like a door.
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.1: You came along the pier... and the salt didn't take you. I'm Ylva. My father is Brann, the whaler. He's up at the Costillar, still hunting the Old One. From up there he can't see the harbour... he's forgotten the way home.
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.2: Take my lantern. Tomé lit it from the lighthouse... cold fire, the only fire left in Varado. Carry it close when you go up. If he sees this light, he'll know it's the pier.
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.3: The sea left all at once, like someone drank it. Everyone ran down to the sand to pick up what it left behind. I was up in the lighthouse with Tomé. He wouldn't let me go down. He saved me... and I've been sitting here ever since.
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.4: Then I'll keep the light burning a while longer. Someone has to.
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.5: Is the light still burning? Show it to him, up on the bones. He'll lower that harpoon. I know he will.
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.6: You came back. Will you go up to the Costillar now?
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.7: That's... that's his lantern. Then he's gone. Did he... did he even see the light?
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.8: I saw it. Up on the bones, a light answered mine... and then it went out, slowly, like a lamp at dawn. He saw it. He saw it.
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.9: Give it here. I'll hang them together at the end of the pier, his and mine. Now the boats will know the way home.
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.10: Keep my lantern. It still holds Tomé's cold fire. When you fall, let it bring you back.
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.11: You'd keep it? Then give me back my light. His side of the pier stays dark... and I'll keep waiting.
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.12: The pier is still dark on his side. But mine is burning.
darkcraft.dialogo.ylva.13: Where did you find that lantern? That's my father's. Tell me... did he see the light?
darkcraft.ballenero.voz.6: ...That light. That's the pier light. Ylva? Is that you, girl?
darkcraft.ballenero.voz.7: Forty years... and you kept it burning. Put the kettle on, lass. I'm coming home.
darkcraft.mision.ylva.pendiente: Ylva sits at the end of the jetty of the Stranded Harbour, a cold-fire lantern in her lap. Her father, Brann the whaler, is still at the Whale's Ribcage and has forgotten the way home. You can still help her.
darkcraft.mision.ylva.buscar: Ylva lent you her cold-fire lantern. Take it to the Whale's Ribcage, to the north, where her father Brann is still harpooning the Old One. When he is badly hurt, let him see the light up close: he might remember the way home.
darkcraft.mision.ylva.calma: Brann saw the pier light, lowered his harpoon and went in peace. His lantern lies in the sand of the Ribcage: take it to Ylva.
darkcraft.mision.ylva.volver: Brann fell fighting. You carry his lantern, the one left in the sand of the Ribcage. Go back to Ylva, at the end of the jetty... and decide whether to give it to her.
darkcraft.mision.ylva.volver_luz: Brann saw the pier light and went in peace. You carry his lantern: go back to Ylva, at the end of the jetty... and decide whether to give it to her.
darkcraft.mision.ylva.encontrada: An old whaler's lantern, brass crusted with salt, in the sand of the Ribcage. In the Stranded Harbour, at the end of the jetty, someone keeps a light burning.
darkcraft.mision.ylva.dada: You gave Ylva her father's lantern. She hung them together at the end of the pier, his and hers, and at last she rested. She left you her cold fire.
darkcraft.mision.ylva.quedada: You kept Brann's lantern and gave Ylva back her light. His side of the pier stays dark; she is still waiting.
darkcraft.mision.ylva.ir.pendiente: Ylva, at the end of the jetty of the Stranded Harbour
darkcraft.mision.ylva.ir.calma: Brann's lantern, in the sand of the Ribcage
darkcraft.mision.ylva.ir.volver: Ylva waits at the end of the jetty
darkcraft.mision.ylva.ir.volver_luz: Ylva waits at the end of the jetty
darkcraft.mision.ylva.ir.encontrada: A light at the end of the jetty of the Stranded Harbour
darkcraft.mision.ylva.cogido: You have Brann's lantern: go back to Ylva, at the end of the jetty of the Stranded Harbour.
darkcraft.mision.ylva.cogido_sin: An old whaler's lantern, cold. Someone was waiting for it to be lit...
darkcraft.mision.ylva.nada: There is nothing left to take.
darkcraft.talisman.ylva.guarda: Ylva's cold fire keeps your echoes.
item.darkcraft.farol_ylva.desc: A small black-iron lantern with the lighthouse's cold fire: blue, almost white at the heart, and it does not burn. Tomé lit it the night the sea left. If Brann sees this light, he'll know it's the pier.
item.darkcraft.farol_ballenero.desc: The whaler's oil lantern, green brass crusted with salt and smoked glass. Forty years lighting the hunt for a whale that was already gone.
item.darkcraft.talisman_ylva.desc: If you fall again before recovering your sword of light, its echoes are not lost: they pass to the new one.
item.darkcraft.talisman_ballenero.desc: Enemies within 24 blocks can be seen through walls.
subtitles.darkcraft.sfx.brann_calma: A whale sings and the sea returns
subtitles.darkcraft.sfx.ylva_descansa: A calm sea and two lanterns
advancements.darkcraft.ylva_luz.title: Two Lanterns
advancements.darkcraft.ylva_farol.title: His Side Stays Dark
advancements.darkcraft.brann_calma.title: Coming Home
advancements.darkcraft.brann_calma.descr: Let Brann see the pier light before he falls
darkcraft.diario.ylva_luz: I gave Ylva her father's lantern. She hung them together at the end of the jetty, his and hers; she said the boats would know the way home now. Then she sat looking at the sea that isn't there, and faded like a light at dawn. She left me her cold fire.
darkcraft.diario.ylva_farol: I kept Brann's lantern and gave Ylva back her light. She still sits at the end of the jetty of the Stranded Harbour. Her side of the pier is burning; his stays dark.
darkcraft.diario.brann_calma: I took the pier light to the Ribcage. Brann saw it among the bones, lowered his harpoon and asked for his daughter. He asked her to put the kettle on, that he was coming home. And he crumbled into salt, slowly.
darkcraft.ayuda.ylva: Ylva and Brann's lanterns: where they are, take you to her or to the lantern in the sand, place them now or forget them
darkcraft.dialogo.corwen.1: Careful on those planks, they're rotten through. Not many come out this far into the fog. I'm Corwen. I was the lamplighter here. Every night I lit the three beacons of the marsh... so the boats could find their way home.
darkcraft.dialogo.corwen.2: You'd do that for an old man? Here... my tinderbox. One beacon at the end of the jetty, one on the western islet, one by the drowned chapel. Light all three... and listen for the bells.
darkcraft.dialogo.corwen.3: The night the sky turned red, the fog came in thick as wool, and it smelled of blood. The boats were still out. I lit the first beacon... and the wind blew it out. My hands shook too much to light it again. I heard their bells out there all night. Then nothing.
darkcraft.dialogo.corwen.4: Then I'll sit with the dark a while longer. It's good company, once you get used to it.
darkcraft.dialogo.corwen.5: Still dark out there? The jetty, the western islet, the drowned chapel. And keep away from the ones floating in the water.
darkcraft.dialogo.corwen.6: You came back. Will you light them now?
darkcraft.dialogo.corwen.7: I see them... three lights in the fog, just like before. Do you hear that? Bells. Boat bells. They're coming home. Should I... should I go down and meet them?
darkcraft.dialogo.corwen.8: Then I'll go down to the water. Keep my lantern, friend. It never once lost its way in the fog.
darkcraft.dialogo.corwen.9: Aye, you're right. Someone has to keep the light, and I've kept it this long. Take my pole... my arms are too old for it now. Yours aren't.
darkcraft.dialogo.corwen.10: Three lights, every night. I trim the wicks and I listen. Some nights I almost hear them laughing out there.
darkcraft.mision.corwen.pendiente: Corwen, the old lamplighter of the Stilt Village, sits on a crate at the end of the walkway from the Reed Islet. The night the sky turned red he could not light the marsh beacons, and the boats never came home. You can still help him.
darkcraft.mision.corwen.buscar: Corwen gave you his tinderbox. Light the three marsh beacons: at the end of the jetty, on the western islet and on the islet by the drowned chapel. Beware of the ones floating in the water.
darkcraft.mision.corwen.una: One beacon burns in the fog. Two to go (the jetty, the western islet or the one by the drowned chapel); the compass leads you to the nearest.
darkcraft.mision.corwen.dos: Two beacons burn in the fog. One to go; the compass leads you to it.
darkcraft.mision.corwen.volver: All three beacons burn, and bells have rung in the fog. Go back to Corwen, at the end of the walkway.
darkcraft.mision.corwen.ida: You let Corwen go down to the water to meet the boats. He was lost in the fog, among the bells. He left you his lantern.
darkcraft.mision.corwen.queda: You asked Corwen to stay and keep the light. He is still on his crate, trimming the wicks of the three beacons. He gave you his pole.
darkcraft.mision.corwen.ir.pendiente: Corwen, at the end of the walkway from the Reed Islet
darkcraft.mision.corwen.ir.buscar: An unlit beacon of the Stilt Village
darkcraft.mision.corwen.ir.una: An unlit beacon of the Stilt Village
darkcraft.mision.corwen.ir.volver: Corwen waits at the end of the walkway
darkcraft.mision.corwen.apagada: An unlit beacon, cold and black with soot. You need something to light it with.
darkcraft.mision.corwen.encendida: The beacon burns in the fog (%s of 3).
darkcraft.mision.corwen.todas: All three beacons burn. Far away, in the fog, bells are ringing.
item.darkcraft.yesquero.desc: A little tin box with dry tinder, a flint and a steel striker worn down by years of lighting. It lights the marsh beacons.
item.darkcraft.pertiga_farolero.desc: Corwen's ash pole, with the brass hook he hung the lanterns from and an iron tip. The hook still holds embers: sometimes it sets what it strikes on fire.
item.darkcraft.talisman_farolero.desc: It never once lost its way in the fog. Those who lie in wait, lying down, floating or praying, don't notice you until you're almost upon them.
subtitles.darkcraft.sfx.corwen_se_va: Footsteps into the water, toward the fog
advancements.darkcraft.balizas.title: Three Lights in the Fog
advancements.darkcraft.balizas.descripti: Light the three beacons of the Stilt Village
advancements.darkcraft.corwen_barcas.des: Let Corwen go down to meet the boats
advancements.darkcraft.corwen_luz.title: Someone Has to Keep the Light
advancements.darkcraft.corwen_luz.descri: Ask Corwen to stay and keep the light
darkcraft.diario.balizas: I lit the three marsh beacons with Corwen's tinderbox: the one on the jetty, the one on the western islet and the one by the drowned chapel. When the last one caught, bells rang in the fog, far away over the water.
darkcraft.diario.corwen_barcas: I told Corwen to go and meet the boats. He got up from his crate, gave me his lantern and waded slowly into the water, toward the bells, until the fog took him.
darkcraft.diario.corwen_luz: I asked Corwen to stay and keep the light. He gave me his pole and stayed on his crate, the lantern burning at his feet, listening for boats that never come.
darkcraft.ayuda.corwen: Corwen and the Stilt Village beacons: where they are, take you to him or to a beacon, place them now or forget them
darkcraft.dialogo.sigrun.1: Halt. No one passes the Fang while I stand. ...You're not one of them. Marked... I can see it on you. I am Sigrun, Warden of the Pass. My oath holds me here... until someone strikes me down.
darkcraft.dialogo.sigrun.2: Then draw your blade. Fight me with everything you have... and don't you dare hold back.
darkcraft.dialogo.sigrun.3: When the Capital burned, my captain sent us to hold this pass, so the people could flee to the monastery. We held it. Nine days. My brothers fell one by one... I swore no one would pass while I stood. I'm still standing.
darkcraft.dialogo.sigrun.4: Then go back the way you came. The pass stays closed.
darkcraft.dialogo.sigrun.5: You again. Have you found your courage?
darkcraft.dialogo.sigrun.6: Enough... enough. You've beaten me. The oath... is broken.
darkcraft.dialogo.sigrun.7: Nine days and a lifetime... and you finally put me on my knees. My oath is fulfilled. Now finish it... or let me go. The choice is yours.
darkcraft.dialogo.sigrun.8: Thank you. Tell them... the pass held.
darkcraft.dialogo.sigrun.9: Let me go? Then I'll go down to the monastery and find their names. All nine of them. Take my shield. I won't need it where I'm going.
darkcraft.dialogo.sigrun.10: You fell. There's no shame in that. When you're ready... I'll be here. I'm always here.
darkcraft.mision.sigrun.titulo: The Duel of the Fang Pass
darkcraft.mision.sigrun.pendiente: Sigrun, Warden of the Pass, lets no one cross the Fang Pass, in the Snowy Mountains, while she still stands. She swore to hold it until someone strikes her down, and she has challenged you to a duel.
darkcraft.mision.sigrun.duelo: You accepted Sigrun's duel. Go back to the pass and fight her with everything you have.
darkcraft.mision.sigrun.caido: You fell before Sigrun. "There's no shame in that", she said. She is still at the pass, waiting until you are ready.
darkcraft.mision.sigrun.vencida: You put Sigrun on her knees: her oath is fulfilled. She asked you to finish her or to let her go. She is still at the pass.
darkcraft.mision.sigrun.rematada: You finished Sigrun. "Tell them... the pass held." The snow took her among the swords of her nine brothers. You kept her sword.
darkcraft.mision.sigrun.libre: You let Sigrun go. She climbed up the pass, toward the monastery, to find the names of her nine brothers. She gave you her shield.
darkcraft.mision.sigrun.ir.duelo: Sigrun waits for you at the Fang Pass
darkcraft.mision.sigrun.ir.caido: Sigrun waits for you at the Fang Pass
item.darkcraft.espada_guardiana.desc: Sigrun's longsword. It held the Fang Pass for nine days and a lifetime, and the steel is still as cold as the snow of the pass.
item.darkcraft.espada_guardiana.frio: Each strike adds frost: the fifth one freezes (bosses, half as much).
item.darkcraft.escudo_guardiana.desc: Sigrun's teardrop shield, night blue with the white fang of the pass and frost stuck to its rim. "I won't need it where I'm going."
darkcraft.escudo.guardiana: It stops everything and, raised at the right instant, stops the whole blow and staggers the attacker.
darkcraft.bestiario.sigrun.desc: The last of the ten the captain of the Capital sent to hold the Fang Pass so the people could flee to the monastery. They held it nine days; her brothers fell one by one and she swore no one would pass while she stood. She attacks no one: she challenges you to a duel. Behind her teardrop shield she stops almost everything from the front (arrows, all of it): strike her while she attacks or from the sides, and don't hit her shield too many times in a row, or she answers with a shield bash. Her lunge crosses half the pass. Wounded, she spins with her sword outstretched and leaps to land with it in the snow. She does not die: she yields.
subtitles.darkcraft.sfx.sigrun_salto: Sigrun lands with her sword in the snow
advancements.darkcraft.sigrun.title: Nine Days and a Lifetime
advancements.darkcraft.sigrun.descriptio: Defeat Sigrun, Warden of the Pass, in her duel
advancements.darkcraft.sigrun_paso.title: The Pass Held
advancements.darkcraft.sigrun_paso.descr: Finish Sigrun when she asks you to
darkcraft.diario.sigrun: At the Fang Pass, Sigrun, Warden of the Pass, challenged me to a duel. We fought in the snow, among the swords of her nine brothers, until she fell to her knees: "Enough... You've beaten me. The oath is broken."
darkcraft.diario.sigrun_paso: Sigrun asked me to finish her or to let her go. I finished her. "Thank you. Tell them... the pass held." She lay in the snow with her sword on her chest, and the snow took her. I kept her sword.
darkcraft.diario.sigrun_nombres: Sigrun asked me to finish her or to let her go. I let her go. She stood up, saluted me with her sword and climbed up the pass, toward the monastery, to find the names of her nine brothers. She gave me her shield: she won't need it where she's going.
darkcraft.ayuda.sigrun: Sigrun and her duel: how she is, take you to her, place or forget her, start the duel, leave her at half health, make her yield, finish her or let her go, send her back to her post or make her do an action
darkcraft.bestiario.enterrado_picador.de: The night shift of the Black Iron Mines was below when the sky turned red and the mountain shook. No one came up. They are still digging, grey with iron dust, the lamp still lit on their brow. Their eyes are white with dust: they cannot see, they hear. Run and they will hear you from afar; crouch and you can walk right past them. The pick blow comes down from above and hooks your shield: if you block it, your guard breaks. Better to step aside. Arrows barely get in; hammers do.
The blasters opened the galleries with powder. Now they throw their charges at whatever they hear: the charge lands, the fuse sputters for a moment and it bursts. Get away before the flame reaches the powder; it does not spare their own either. Up close they strike with the lit fuse. When they die, their satchel sometimes catches: if you hear it sputter, step back.
darkcraft.bestiario.enterrado_cargador.d: The haulers carried the ore up in baskets on their backs. They are huge and slow, and they carry a sledgehammer. The sledge blow makes the ground shake: jump or roll to escape the shockwave. They also sweep wide and charge with the shoulder. A heavy blow near a broken ceiling brings it down; anyone can be caught under it, them too.
darkcraft.mina.escotilla_cerrada: The hatch is locked from below.
darkcraft.morvain.cama: There is no sleeping in Morvain.
advancements.darkcraft.minas.title: The Night Shift
advancements.darkcraft.minas.description: Go down into the Black Iron Mines
advancements.darkcraft.enterrado.title: Blind in the Dark
darkcraft.diario.minas: At the foot of the Snowy Mountains, facing the Faithless Land, lie the Black Iron Mines: an open pit cut in steps, a headframe with its wheel above the shaft and, at the bottom, the mine mouth. The chains that hold the citadel were forged from their iron. In the lamp room, the wall of lamp hooks is almost empty.
darkcraft.diario.enterrado: The Buried Ones are the night shift of the mines. They cannot see: they hear. The pickmen dig at the rock and break your guard with the pick, the blasters throw charges that burst soon after landing and the haulers make the ground shake with the sledgehammer. If you don't run, they don't hear you.
darkcraft.ayuda.mina: The Black Iron Mines: go to one of its places, its Buried Ones, bring down a broken ceiling, open or close the headframe hatch or the chapel wall
darkcraft.capataz.voz.1: Who's there? The shift isn't over... Back to the vein! Everyone, back to work!
darkcraft.capataz.voz.2: The vein... it's mine! It always was! Dig, you dogs... DIG!
darkcraft.capataz.voz.3: Another one for the shaft. Forty lamps went down... forty-one, now.
darkcraft.capataz.voz.4: Light the charges! Blow the wall!
darkcraft.capataz.voz.5: The lamps... I can see the lamps... going up... Let them... go home.
subtitles.darkcraft.sfx.capataz_roca: A rock falls from the ceiling
item.darkcraft.pico_capataz.desc: Hakon's double pick of black iron, with the red vein set into its head. He opened level three with it; the vein is still alive inside.
item.darkcraft.pico_capataz.veta: Each strike leaves crystal in its target: the fourth in a row bursts and also hurts those around it.
darkcraft.bestiario.capataz.desc: The night-shift foreman of the Black Iron Mines. He opened level three, where the red vein bleeds, and ordered the wall blown open where voices could be heard behind it. On the night of the red sky he stayed below, in the Cavern of the Lode, with the vein inside him, and he still digs at its heart. His pick breaks your guard if you block it with a shield; he sweeps very wide and charges with his crystal shoulder. When he drives the pick into the ground, the vein erupts in a line toward you: step aside. He lights charges at his lantern and throws them in a fan. If he strikes the ground twice, rocks fall from the ceiling: get out of the mark. With his whistle he calls the shift. At half health he drinks the vein: he glows, moves faster and crystals burst around him.
advancements.darkcraft.capataz.title: The Last Shift
advancements.darkcraft.capataz.descripti: Defeat Hakon, the Foreman, in the Cavern of the Lode
darkcraft.diario.capataz: In the Cavern of the Lode, deep in the Black Iron Mines, Hakon, the foreman, was still digging at the heart of the vein. The vein had gotten inside him: red crystals grew from his shoulder and arm. When he fell he stayed on his knees, leaning on his pick, and watched the forty lamps of the night shift rise: "Let them... go home." The mines went silent.
darkcraft.ayuda.capataz: Hakon, the Foreman: how he is, take you to the Cavern of the Lode, defeat him, bring him back, make him drink the vein, make him do an action or let him choose again
darkcraft.bestiario.ensamblado_portaciri: The Assembled Ones are the forty thousand of the Ossuary of Saint Ulf, raised on the night of the red sky, but mixed up: one man's skull, another's arms, a third one's ribs. The candlebearer carries a candelabrum of bones with its candles lit: its strike and its sweep set you on fire. When it falls, it comes apart into a heap of bones and five seconds later it puts itself back together, with half its health. To stop it rising again, strike the heap before it gets up, or kill it with fire or with a hammer.
darkcraft.bestiario.ensamblado_sepulture: The gravediggers are still digging in the churchyard with Brother Osmund's shovels. The shovel blow reaches far and, if you are a few steps away, they throw earth in your eyes: it blinds you for a moment and slows you down. Like every Assembled One, when they fall they come apart into bones and soon rise again if no one crushes the heap; fire and hammers turn them to dust.
darkcraft.bestiario.ensamblado_coloso.de: Brother Osmund put together in a single body the bones he could not match to anyone: the colossus, twice as tall as a man, with a mace made from a giant's thighbone. It is slow and very hard to bring down. Its mace blow makes the ground shake around it (jump or roll) and, if you stay too close, it stomps. It also rises again after falling: do not stray from the heap.
darkcraft.osario.pisotea: The bones are moving: strike the heap before it rises.
darkcraft.osario.escotilla_cerrada: The tomb's trapdoor is locked from below.
advancements.darkcraft.osario.title: Forty Thousand
advancements.darkcraft.osario.descriptio: Go down into the crypt of the Ossuary of Saint Ulf
advancements.darkcraft.ensamblado.title: Dust Thou Art
advancements.darkcraft.ensamblado.descri: Turn an Assembled One to dust
darkcraft.diario.osario: In the Dead Forest, on a knoll among leafless trees, lies the churchyard of Saint Ulf: open graves, wooden crosses and a roofless chapel with its cracked bell. Behind the altar, the stairs go down into the crypt. Eighty years before the red sky, the Grey Plague filled the churchyard, and Brother Osmund, the sacristan, dug up the forty thousand and kept their bones below, in order. Down there is a chapel made of bones.
darkcraft.diario.ensamblado: The Assembled Ones do not die the first time: they come apart into a heap of bones and soon put themselves back together. You have to strike the bones before they rise, or burn them, or smash them with a hammer. Then, yes: dust.
darkcraft.ayuda.osario: The Ossuary of Saint Ulf: go to one of its places, its Assembled Ones, open or close the tomb's trapdoor or the priors' wall, ring the cracked bell or bring out an Assembled One (and undo or rebuild the nearest one)
darkcraft.osmund.voz.1: Thirty-nine thousand... nine hundred... Who is there? You walk upon the counted. Lie down... and be counted too.
darkcraft.osmund.voz.2: Brothers! Sisters! Rise! Hold me up... as I held every one of you!
darkcraft.osmund.voz.3: Another one... skull, ribs, thighbones... all in order. Always in order.
darkcraft.osmund.voz.4: Bow your heads... before the dead!
darkcraft.osmund.voz.5: I have lost the count... Forgive me... I have lost... the count...
subtitles.darkcraft.sfx.osmund_corona: The crown of skulls breaks loose
item.darkcraft.incensario_sacristan.desc: Brother Osmund's bronze censer, on its chain. Inside, the bone dust he burned for the forty thousand still smolders.
item.darkcraft.incensario_sacristan.bras: Each strike scatters bone dust that slows; the third in a row stirs the embers and sets those around ablaze.
darkcraft.bestiario.osmund.desc: The sacristan of the Ossuary of Saint Ulf. When the Grey Plague filled the churchyard he dug up the dead and laid their bones in the crypt, forty thousand, counted one by one; he died counting and was buried at Saint Ulf's feet. On the night of the red sky he rose, made of the bones of many, with a halo of bones and skulls on his back. He smashes his censer down before him (the burning dust slows and weakens) and whirls it around him (it burns). The skulls of his halo break loose, orbit him and fly at you: step aside or shatter them with a blow. He plunges his hands down and bones erupt in a fan; he raises his arms and garlands of bones fall from the dome: get out of the mark. With his bell he raises the dead from their heaps. At half health the dead hold him up in the air. Hammers break his bones.
advancements.darkcraft.osmund.title: The Lost Count
advancements.darkcraft.osmund.descriptio: Defeat Brother Osmund, the Sacristan, in the Reliquary
darkcraft.diario.osmund: In the Reliquary, beneath the Chapel of Bones, Brother Osmund was still counting: thirty-nine thousand nine hundred... When he fell he stayed on his knees, his censer on the floor, and at last he lost the count. The souls of the forty thousand rose up through the dome, and the bones of the ossuary lay still.
darkcraft.ayuda.osmund: Brother Osmund, the Sacristan: how he is, take you to the Reliquary, defeat him, bring him back, make him rise, make him do an action or let him choose again
darkcraft.bestiario.destilado_mancebo.de: Master Galen's apprentices drank his elixir so as not to fall ill; now their beaked masks have grown into their faces. From afar they lob flasks: the fire flask leaves the ground burning and the acid flask a corrosive puddle (that also wears down your armor). If one of their own is hurt, they throw it the green elixir, which heals it: kill them first. Up close they strike with the mortar's pestle.
darkcraft.bestiario.destilado_enfermo.de: The victims of the Grey Plague that Galen treated with his elixir: grey skin, filthy bandages and green glass boils that glimmer in the dark. They wait sitting on the floor or lying beside the stretchers, like one more patient. They are fast: their claws poison you, they pounce from a few steps away and they spit out what they carry inside (it poisons too). Ash fruits cure the poison.
darkcraft.bestiario.destilado_cuba.desc: The strongest ones Galen used as vats: they carry on their backs a glass vat full of distillate, with tubes that enter through their shoulders. They are slow and very hard to bring down. They punch, charge from afar and bend over so the vat pours its acid out in front of them: get out of the fan. When they fall their vat bursts, and the green puddle heals any Distilled One that steps in it: lead the others away from there.
darkcraft.lazareto.hundida: The stairs have collapsed. The shaft in the middle of the tower goes all the way up...
darkcraft.lazareto.atanor: The athanor roars: hot air rises up the tower's shaft.
advancements.darkcraft.lazareto.title: Quarantine
advancements.darkcraft.lazareto.descript: Enter the tower of Master Galen's Lazaretto
advancements.darkcraft.atanor.title: Updraft
advancements.darkcraft.atanor.descriptio: Light the athanor in the Lazaretto's cellar
advancements.darkcraft.destilado.title: Bitter Medicine
darkcraft.diario.lazareto: In the south of the Rotting Marsh, on an islet in the middle of a lagoon, stands Master Galen's Lazaretto: a round tower of dark stone with copper bands and a dome of green glass. When the Grey Plague reached the marsh, Galen, the physician the Academy had cast out, brought the sick there by boat and gave them what he distilled to drink. They did not die. They stayed.
darkcraft.diario.atanor: In the Lazaretto's cellar is the athanor, Galen's furnace, beneath a shaft that rises through the middle of the tower. I pulled the lever and the fire caught: the hot air rushes up the shaft so strongly that it carried me upwards, floor by floor. Crouching, you come down slowly.
darkcraft.diario.destilado: Galen's Distilled have grey skin and boils of green glass. The apprentices, in their beaked masks, throw flasks of fire and acid, and a green one to their own kind that heals them: kill them first. The living vats' glass bursts when they fall, and what spills out heals the others: you have to lead them away from there.
darkcraft.ayuda.lazareto: Master Galen's Lazaretto: go to one of its places, its Distilled, light or put out the athanor, open or close the library wall or bring out a Distilled One
